estate.does_not_work: Does not work: outside the labour force
estate.flight_event: Private jet flight from the estate: {tonnes} t CO2
estate.flights_line: Flights this game: {flights}, {tonnes} t CO2 in all. The whole town has emitted {town_tonnes} t so far.
estate.grounded_note: The jet is grounded while the pilot is let go.

estate.top_share_line: {name} (1 of {households} households, {people} of {total_people} people) holds {top} of the town's {total} net worth.
estate.wealth_tax_note: Paid in part if the estate's savings cannot cover it
estate.wealth_tax_short: Wealth tax paid in part: about {owed} was due and {paid} was paid, because the estate's savings ({savings}) fall short.

finance_hint.bank-cr: Equity over loans. Must stay above the limit, or lending stops.
finance_hint.bank-head: How much more the bank can lend before it hits the capital limit.
finance_hint.f-rev: Money received for purchases, from the ledger. Up to about 10% below the model's own firm revenue: a firm buying from itself moves no money.
finance_hint.hh-save: Share of income left after tax, rent, loan payments and spending.
finance_hint.revenue.capitalTax: Capital tax: charged on income from owning things (dividends, rent, interest) that households receive.
finance_hint.revenue.profitTax: Profit tax: charged on a firm's profit each month, before dividends are paid out to its owners.
finance_hint.revenue.wageTax: Income tax: charged on the wages households earn (the lever key is still tax_wage).

inspect.building: Removal is queued like any move and costs political capital.
inspect.commons: Change access and harvest in the policy drawer.
inspect.empty: Pick a building or a road in the build palette to place one here.
inspect.fire_station_effect: fires there burn shorter and spread less
inspect.firm_inactive: No firm has been founded here yet. Firms open when households move up in class.
inspect.forest_burning: Burning forest stops absorbing carbon. A fire station nearby shortens fires and slows their spread.
inspect.forest_regrowing: Burnt tiles regrow slowly and then stand again.
inspect.forest_standing: Forests are fixed scenery in this version.
inspect.palette_fire_station: Covers forest within about {radius} tiles: shorter, slower fires.
inspect.palette_fire_station_help: Click free ground, ideally next to the forest. Forest within about {radius} tiles burns for a shorter time and spreads less; a ring on the map shows the cover. Esc to stop.
inspect.planned_draft: Cancel it from the plan tray.
inspect.planned_queued: Cancel it from the pending list to get half the political capital back.
inspect.road: A commute over a road tile takes less time than over open ground.

ledger.external_bank credit creation: Money the bank creates when it lends: the borrower's balance and debt both rise.
ledger.external_bank credit destruction: Money that disappears when a loan is repaid: the payer's balance and debt both fall.
ledger.external_other: An account outside the town (no ledger).
ledger.firm_revenue_note: Revenue on the ledger is money actually received. It can sit up to about 10% below the Revenue figure of the firm's books, because when the Factory buys capital goods from itself the model records a sale but no money moves.

lobby.note: You set {set}; lobbying is expected to leave about {expected} in force (this opposes the change).

metric_hint.avg_income: Total household income per person per month, children and retired people included
metric_hint.budget: Share of the carbon budget not yet used
metric_hint.climate_stress: Rises as the carbon budget runs down. The more stress, the likelier and fiercer fires and droughts become.
metric_hint.commons_health: Health of the shared land. Droughts and over-harvesting wear it down.
metric_hint.debt: Government debt relative to a year of output
metric_hint.emissions: Net emissions in the latest month: sources minus the forest sink. Open "how?" for the turn total, the accumulated total and the sources.
metric_hint.farm_health: How well the farm can produce. It follows forest and commons health and drops in a drought.
metric_hint.forest: Forest stock, as a share of its maximum
metric_hint.forest_health: How much of the forest is still standing and healthy. Fires burn it down; burnt tiles regrow slowly.
metric_hint.gini: 0 is perfectly equal, 1 is one person has everything
metric_hint.gpi: Genuine progress: output adjusted for social and environmental costs
metric_hint.legitimacy: Public trust in government; at zero the town collapses
metric_hint.median_income: The middle person: half the town earns more, half less. Compare with the average to see skew
metric_hint.temperature: Degrees C above the starting level
metric_hint.top_wealth_share: Share of all household net worth held by the single richest household
metric_hint.unemployment: Share of the labour force without a job
metric_hint.wage_share: Share of income paid as wages

misc.energy_unit_help: {unit}: energy per month, in megawatt-hours. The unit is a label from the game's settings; the numbers are the model's own.
misc.gst_reason: Households buy goods and services untaxed: the model taxes income, profit, capital, wealth and carbon, but a sales tax would need a price-and-purchase layer it does not have. Government revenue therefore has no GST line.

story.budget_full: and to {full} left, where stress is at its fullest, by {when}
story.budget_never: The carbon budget never fell low enough to start climate stress ({used} used at the end).
story.budget_onset: The carbon budget fell to {onset} left, where climate stress starts, by {when}
story.stress_never: Climate stress never began: the town kept more than {onset} of its carbon budget, so there were no fires or droughts.

weather.forecast_adapt: A fire station near the forest and resilience spending both lower the risk.
weather.forecast_none: No climate stress yet, so no fires or droughts are expected.
weather.forecast_quiet: Nothing unusual is expected this quarter.
weather.health_commons: Health of the shared land. Droughts and over-harvesting wear it down.
weather.health_farm: How well the farm can produce: it follows forest and commons health, and falls in a drought.
weather.health_forest: Share of the forest still standing. Fires burn it and the carbon sink shrinks with it.
weather.lens_note: Per-tile chance that a fire starts there this month, from the simulation. The colours are scaled to the riskiest tile.
weather.stress_active: Weather is more erratic and fires and droughts are likelier. Full stress at {full} budget left.
weather.stress_none: No climate stress yet: erratic weather begins when {onset} of the carbon budget is left.

systems.name: Market capitalism
systems.tagline: Owners keep the profits; wages follow the labour market.

facts.label: Wages
facts.value: Set by the market (a reserve army of unemployed holds them down)

systems.resistance: Not described in the design doc.

tradeoffs.label: Strength
tradeoffs.value: Fast growth driven by profit and investment (the growth loop in the design doc).

tradeoffs.label: Cost
tradeoffs.value: Growth also drives emissions up, and wealth can capture policy through lobbying.

systems.name: Regulated capitalism
systems.tagline: Owners still profit, but wages have a higher floor and lobbying is capped.

facts.label: Wages
facts.value: Market wages with a higher floor

facts.label: Unlocks
facts.value: A campaign-spending cap and community management of the commons

tradeoffs.label: Strength
tradeoffs.value: Unlocks the campaign-spending cap and community management of the commons, and lowers the ceiling on lobbying. The emissions cap works in every system.

tradeoffs.label: Cost
tradeoffs.value: A long transition with some output lost while it lasts.

tradeoffs.label: Trade-off
tradeoffs.value: Lower GDP growth than market capitalism, in return for a better chance of staying inside the carbon budget (a design target, not a promise).

systems.name: Worker cooperatives
systems.tagline: Employees share the surplus and own the firms.

facts.label: Wages
facts.value: A share of surplus, with a floor

facts.label: Credit
facts.value: Banks distrust co-ops: a spread is added

systems.resistance: High resistance. The doc does not say from whom; expect owners and lenders.

tradeoffs.label: Strength
tradeoffs.value: Profits go to workers, which pulls inequality down, and lobbying power is lowest.

tradeoffs.label: Cost
tradeoffs.value: A long transition with some output lost while it lasts; workers need training.

tradeoffs.label: Trade-off
tradeoffs.value: Slower growth, and not a free pass on emissions.

kinds.title: Households and people
kinds.summary: Nine households of people. A household decides how much of its money to spend each month and which shop gets it. People do not choose jobs one by one: firms hire from the unemployed (cheapest reservation wage first, ties to higher skill). A household's class is a label worked out from what it owns and earns; it is never chosen.
decides: How much to spend on food, goods and services this month
Which firm in each sector gets that spending
Whether to found a firm in the dormant slot (a Worker or Manager household with enough savings)
Capital-owning households: how much to give lobbying
observes: Its savings and last disposable income
The interest rate, firms' profit and unmet demand (for founding a firm)
kinds.rule: food = min(need x food price, savings); discretionary = min(propensity x max(0, disposable - food need) + wealth spending, savings - food); services = services share x discretionary; goods = the rest. Shop weight = stock x (average price / price) ^ elasticity, where the average price is weighted by stock

params.label: Share of discretionary spending on services
Capitalists and Rentiers: spending out of wealth
params.unit: share of net wealth per month

variants.label: Capitalist
variants.decision: Owns firms or the bank and lives mostly on profit; spends only part of income and funds lobbying.
variants.rule: owns assets and capital share of recent income above the threshold, rent not the main part

variants.label: Rentier
variants.decision: Lives mostly on rent from homes it lets; spends part of income and funds lobbying.
variants.rule: as Capitalist, but rent received is above the rentier share of capital income

variants.label: Manager
variants.decision: Skilled and well paid; spends most of income and is the person who receives lobbying money.
variants.rule: employed, top skill above the skill threshold and pay above the skilled wage ratio times the base wage

variants.label: Worker
variants.decision: Lives on wages; spends nearly all income, buying food first.

variants.label: Dependent
variants.decision: No one in the household has a job; lives on benefits and savings, food first.
variants.rule: no employed member, and not a Capitalist or Rentier

classParams.label: Capital share of income that makes a Capitalist or Rentier
Rent share of capital income that makes a Rentier
Pay needed for a Manager, against the base wage

kinds.title: Firms
kinds.summary: Factory, Farm and Shop, plus one dormant slot a household can start. Each firm decides how many workers it wants, what to pay and what to charge. (Market, Regulated and Coop are not kinds of firm: they are the town-wide economic system the player picks, which changes ownership and payout rules.)
decides: How many workers to have: hire up to a monthly cap, fire after a sustained surplus
The base wage, adjusted each month
How much to invest and borrow
observes: Expected sales (a smoothed average of past demand)
Its inventory and how much cover it wants
Its unit cost (wages plus carbon cost per unit)
kinds.rule: target workers = ceil(labour needed - hire slack), where needed output = expected sales x (1 + growth aspiration) + inventory adjust x (cover x expected sales - inventory); wage step = trend + wage_k x (u_ref - unemployment), capped; price moves a share of the way to (1 + markup) x unit cost; expected sales = smoothing x demand + (1 - smoothing) x previous

params.label: Share of the inventory gap closed per month
Largest wage change in a month
Share of the price gap closed per month
Weight of this month's demand in expected sales

kinds.title: Bank
kinds.summary: One bank that lends to firms against its equity, takes deposits and pays a dividend from excess capital. It follows a rule; it does not weigh individual borrowers.
decides: The interest rate each firm pays
How much a firm may borrow (a leverage cap and the bank's capital ratio)
How much of excess capital to pay out
observes: The base rate set by the player
Each firm's debt against its assets (leverage)
kinds.rule: firm loan rate = base rate + base spread + leverage spread x leverage + system spread; leverage = debt / (capital value + cash); borrowing limited to max leverage x assets

params.label: Base spread over the policy rate
Extra spread per unit of leverage
Share of excess capital paid out

kinds.title: Government
kinds.summary: The government collects taxes, pays benefits and spending and borrows for deficits, all at the levels the player sets. Its own rule is legitimacy: a score that drifts with wellbeing, unemployment, inequality and debt.
decides: Nothing on its own about policy: levers are the player's
How much to borrow or repay to keep a cash target
How much of its spending it can actually fund
observes: Wellbeing, smoothed unemployment, the Gini coefficient and debt against GDP
Whether the bank was bailed out this month
kinds.rule: legitimacy change = wellbeing weight x (wellbeing - 0.5) - unemployment weight x max(0, unemployment - threshold) - inequality weight x max(0, Gini - threshold) - debt weight x max(0, debt/GDP - 1) - bailout penalty

kinds.title: Lobbyists
kinds.summary: Not a separate body: Capitalist and Rentier households give a share of their capital income to the wealthiest Manager household, which acts as the lobbyist. Together with union density this erodes the policies the player sets. The player sees the nominal lever and the effective one.
decides: How much each capital-owning household gives (a share of capital income, up to its savings and the campaign cap)
observes: GDP, wage share and unemployment (for union strength)
kinds.rule: capital pull = lobby k x spend / monthly GDP, capped at the system's maximum; labour pull = union density x wage share x labour weight; net = clamp(capital - labour, 0, max); effective lever = nominal x (1 - net)

params.label: Influence per unit of spending against GDP
Largest net erosion of a lever

kinds.title: Nature
kinds.summary: Forest and commons are not agents: they follow fixed rules for growth, harvest and decay. The one chance event is an owner fencing off an open commons.
decides: Nothing: it responds to emissions, harvest and fire
observes: Cumulative emissions, forest stock, commons use and access rule
kinds.rule: see the Forest and commons topic for growth and the sink; enclosure is a monthly chance while the commons are open

params.label: Monthly chance of enclosure, Market system

kinds.title: Weather
kinds.summary: Droughts and fires are not decisions. Their odds rise with climate stress, which rises as the carbon budget runs down. They are the main place where the random seed matters.
decides: Nothing: odds follow climate stress, dryness and fire stations
observes: Climate stress, forest tiles, drought severity, fire station coverage
kinds.rule: drought chance = base x (1 + gain x stress); ignition chance = base x (1 + gain x stress) x dryness x standing share x (1 - resilience cut); spread chance = spread base x (1 + drought gain x severity) x (1 - station cut)

params.label: Base spread chance per neighbouring forest tile

kinds.title: The estate and its pilot
kinds.summary: One very rich household that does not work, owns the Farm, a posh house, a private jet and a runway. It is an ordinary household for spending, tax and class (it comes out Capitalist), with two extra rules: the jet flies by chance and pays the carbon price, and the estate pays a pilot, who is a worker in another household.
decides: Whether to pay the pilot in full each month (it pays what it holds, up to the wage)
Whether to let the pilot go after months of short pay, and to rehire once it can afford wages again
observes: Its savings, the carbon price after lobbying, whether the pilot is employed
kinds.rule: each month one random draw decides whether the jet flies (only with an employed pilot); a flight adds its tonnes to emissions and charges carbon price x tonnes; the pilot's wage moves from the estate to the pilot's household; unpaid for the maximum number of months: let go; savings cover the rehire months of wages: hired back

params.label: Chance the jet flies in a month

randomness.probability: drought base x (1 + stress gain x climate stress), clamped to 0 to 1
randomness.when: each month with no drought running and climate stress above zero

randomness.event: How severe and how long a drought is
randomness.probability: two uniform draws on 0..1: severity = min(1, sev_min + u x (span base + span stress x stress)); months = dur_min + floor(u x (span base + span stress x stress))

randomness.event: A fire spreads to a neighbouring forest tile
randomness.probability: spread chance x (1 + drought gain x severity) x (1 - station cut if covered)
randomness.when: each month, once for each standing forest tile next to a burning tile

params.label: Cut inside a fire station's reach

randomness.probability: fire base x (1 + stress gain x stress) x dryness x standing forest share x (1 - resilience cut)
randomness.when: each month with climate stress above zero and some forest standing

randomness.probability: one uniform pick among the standing forest tiles
randomness.when: only when a new fire starts

randomness.event: A home next to a fire is damaged
randomness.probability: a fixed chance per home within one tile of a fire
randomness.when: each month for each such home; the draw happens only when the chance is above zero, and in the shipped content it is zero (off)

randomness.event: An owner fences off an open commons
randomness.probability: the economic system's enclosure chance; the richest Capitalist or Rentier household becomes the owner
randomness.when: each month while the commons are open and the chance is above zero (Market only in the shipped content)

randomness.event: A household founds a firm in the dormant slot
randomness.probability: mobility rate x max(0, sector return - base rate), clamped to 0..1
randomness.when: each month when a household has the savings and a dormant slot sits in a sector with enough unmet demand; one draw whatever the odds

params.label: Unmet demand needed in the sector

randomness.probability: the fixed monthly flight chance; the flight happens only if the pilot is employed (the draw is taken either way, so a dismissal never shifts the random stream)
randomness.when: each month while the estate exists

params.label: Chance the jet flies in a month

deterministic: Everything else is deterministic: spending, shop choice, hiring, wages, prices, credit, taxes, lobbying and legitimacy use no random draws.

The seed fixes one stream of random numbers. Changing it changes when droughts and fires happen and where, whether a commons is fenced off, whether a household founds a firm and when the estate's jet flies; it does not change the starting town.
The starting differences between households (income, savings, skill, who owns what) are written in content/initial_town.json, not drawn.
